item.title: OpenAI’s new reasoning technique alarms AI safety experts
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: OpenAI’s new Astra model will use “recurrent depth,” a technique that allows the model to operate outside of the sequential thinking that characterizes most reasoning models.

item.title: MapQuest is now the No. 1 U.S. app after bucking Trump’s ‘Lake America’ renaming
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: The once-dominant mapping app has surged to the top of Apple’s U.S. App Store after refusing to adopt Trump’s “Lake America” name, drawing more than half of its 2026 U.S. downloads in just six days.

item.title: It sure looks like hackers breached a major ID card verification service
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: An identity theft search site claimed to have more than 150 million driver's license photos stolen from an ID verification service. The crime site has now shut down.

item.title: Delivery Hero board backs Uber’s $15B takeover bid
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: If approved, the combined company would become one of the largest food delivery platforms in the world.

item.title: Pangram’s Max Spero on why AI detection is harder than ‘Real or Fake’
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo
item.description: The internet has a trust problem, and it’s not just because social media feeds are filling up with AI slop. AI-generated text and images are now making their way into job applications, product reviews, and even insurance claims, leaving platforms and users alike scrambling to figure out what’s real.  A handful of startups have cropped up in the past couple of […]

item.title: X shifts US creator payouts from Stripe to X Money
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: X says U.S. creator payouts will now be handled through its X Money payments service, a change that appears to replace the previous Stripe-powered payout system.

item.title: US government sides with OpenAI on issue of training LLMs on copyrighted material
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: "The United States has a strong interest in continuing to develop a robust and competitive artificial intelligence industry that sets the standard for the practice and procedure of AI use globally," the brief reads.

item.title: Enhanced geothermal notches another win as Google buys 400 MW from Fervo
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fervo's deal with Google could expand to 1 gigawatt of geothermal power, enough to supply a very large AI data center in Utah.

item.title: Wonderful more than doubles its valuation to $5B in under 6 months
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Wonderful said it will use its $550 million Series C funding to develop products faster, expand its FDE teams, and meet demand for its products.

item.title: India’s richest man now wants to turn aging computers into AI-ready PCs
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Jio is betting it can turn an aging computer into an AI-ready PC for as little as about $11 for two months.

item.title: HiddenLayer nabs $100M as enterprises rush to secure their AI deployments
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Security companies are scrambling to build products that can monitor not just agents but also the tools and add-ons they use.

item.title: PSA: Amazon’s shopping AI can now tell you if that message is a scam
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Amazon is adding a scam-detection feature to Alexa for Shopping that can verify whether suspicious emails, texts, and other messages actually came from the retailer.

item.title: Adobe acquires Indian market intelligence startup Rilo
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: This is Adobe's second acquisition out of India after Rephrase.ai in 2023

item.title: Norway considers ban on camera-enabled wearable ‘pervert glasses’
item.dc:creator: Zack Whittaker
item.description: The Nordic country says wearable camera headsets need to be regulated given their privacy risks.

item.title: Adobe is making its tools available in Slack
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Users will be able to access Express, Premiere, and Acrobat in Slack

item.title: Uber is laying off 10% of staff, or 3,300 people
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Uber is laying off about 3,300 people, or about 10% of its global headcount, in a bid to reduce management layers and invest more in its ridesharing, delivery, and robotaxi divisions.

item.title: OpenAI faces 30 more lawsuits tied to Tumbler Ridge shooting
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: Edelson PC is filing 30 new lawsuits against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge shooting, escalating claims to aiding and abetting and naming Chris Lehane, though evidence remains unconfirmed.

item.title: Larry Page’s flying car company Pivotal loses its CEO
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The company told TechCrunch he is "pursuing new endeavors." Karklin will be replaced on an interim basis by Mike Ross, an aviation executive who joined Pivotal's board of directors in November 2025.

item.title: Reliance’s JioHotstar takes its streaming empire global — without sports
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta, Jagmeet Singh
item.description: JioHotstar will only have entertainment content when it launches in the UK, Canada, and Singapore.

item.title: Apple follows Google in adopting Trump’s ‘Lake America’ name
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Apple Maps is following President Trump's executive order to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America.
